precepts.text: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside. The work of them that turn aside is brothers and sisters that leave the truth. They always say we're still serving God, we still keep the commandments; a year or two later they are back with Easter and Thanksgiving.
precepts.point: And when he could not overcome Onias, he got him to Apollonius the governor of Coelosyria and Phenice. He ran to the other nations. They were working together on this temple, and because of one argument he goes to the other nations against Onias, and told them that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money. You cannot make this stuff up.
precepts.why:
Onias was known for “his hatred of wickedness.” David shows what that hatred looks like: “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; it shall not cleave to me.”

The work of them that turn aside is brothers and sisters that leave the truth. When they leave, they always say, we're still serving God, we keep the commandments, I've been in ministry for 35 years. Everybody says that. But when you see them a year from now, or two years, they are not serving the Lord. They are back with Easter, back with Thanksgiving, back beating piñatas.

God says, I hate the work of them that turn aside, and it shall not cleave to me. That is what Simon of the tribe of Benjamin did: he was the governor of the temple, working with the high priest, and he turned aside. Hating that work, and not letting it cling to you, is part of hating wickedness the way Onias did.

precepts.text: Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off. There is a lot of slander in the Israelite community; some camps thrive off slander, hatred, name calling, ridicule, and false accusations. God already said I am going to cut slanderers off, so for you to join with these people, you are a fool. And they think God is with them.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.
precepts.why:
“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off: him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer.”

There is a lot of slander in the Israelite community; Deacon Asaf has been going over it in classes these last two weeks. There are camps that thrive off slander, hatred, name calling, ridicule and false accusations.

God already told you he is going to cut off people who do that. Cut off means he is going to kill them. So for you to join with these people, you are nothing but a fool.

And the high look and the proud heart come from the slander; that is what they do. They think God is with them, and the men and women around them, as stupid as they are, believe God is with them. God is not with them, not according to these scriptures.

precepts.text: He that uttereth a slander is a fool.
precepts.point: A captain charged after an attack on him and his wife was cleared when video showed he defended himself. Many had already believed the one-sided account.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off”: God will cut you off, cut off from the book of the living. Proverbs shows what is really behind slander: “He that hideth hatred with lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, is a fool.”

When somebody lies on you or slanders you, what that really says is that there is hatred there. The lying lips are hiding hatred.

“and he that uttereth a slander”: you had Tyre Gas, you had Lightfoot, you had these guys uttering slanders, and their followers talk that way because their leaders are the same way. They run with slander. As a leader you are supposed to hear an outrageous lie and say, I do not believe that. One woman said we came to Canada on a magic school bus, and some leaders believed it.

God says you are a fool to listen to lies, run with them and put them out there. Slander is defamation: running with an accusation without two or three witnesses, and God cuts that man off.

precepts.text: A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it.
precepts.point: A captain charged after an attack on him and his wife was cleared when video showed he defended himself. Many had already believed the one-sided account.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.” If you lie on somebody and run with slander, it says that you hate the one who is afflicted by it.

You heard it plainly from one of them: I am here to down IUIC. That is the hatred behind the lying tongue that Psalms 101 says God will cut off.

Every matter is to be established by two or three witnesses. What was put out about Captain Obadiah was one witness, and that witness was a lie. The charges were dropped; the footage and the witnesses showed he was defending himself. It is sad that the white man had to come and say he was defending himself, when those who talk about righteous judgment could not understand something that simple. In London, when our sister died, people said IUIC killed her and hid evidence, and the investigators showed that the man who did it was evil and we had nothing to do with it.

A false witness is called slander, or defamation, and false witness can get you killed. By the law, what was to be done to the brother you slandered is to be done unto you. We do not have power to institute that, but Esau’s court system has defamation, and that is how it is going to be done now: whatever you put out against the truth, you had better be able to prove it, or you will have to come up out of the pockets. That is to protect the ministry of Christ, because the lies are put out to blame the ministry.

precepts.text: Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not.
precepts.point: A captain charged after an attack on him and his wife was cleared when video showed he defended himself. Many had already believed the one-sided account.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.” That is why so many brothers get caught up in suits: striving in things that do not concern them, things they know nothing about. You just hear something and you are running your mouth.

To sit in judgment with sinners is sitting in counsel with brothers that are not right, brothers who were put out of the school, like Judah Mack and Titus.

Read on: “My son, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent.” This is for those who keep running their mouths talking about us. You meddle in matters that do not concern you, and you are not going to be innocent. That is why legal measures are being taken: to teach men to control their mouths, and to make sure that when you say something, it is true.

So the privy slanderer of Psalms 101 is the man who strives in what does not concern him and sits with sinners, and God will cut him off.

moments.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

points: To behave wisely in a perfect way means you apply the laws of God. You read what is written and you do what it says. The laws are the apple of your heart. This is how you're supposed to conduct yourself, how you treat your neighbor, how you treat your brother.

I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: this person got their mind right. I hate the work of them that turn aside from the laws of God, the way of the Most High. I will not know a wicked person: I am not going to put myself around wicked people.

Video played on handling complainers at work: don't come to me with just a complaint; present your solution to me. That's the same thing that distinguishes murmuring from not in the truth: is there a solution? And you don't give your solution to the people that can't implement the solution; you give it to the people that can implement it.

You know how many folks will sit up and complain about some stuff and have absolutely no idea how to fix it or what to do to make it better? But they just feel so good about saying how wrong it is. Where is that going to get us? It doesn't help. So stop.

Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off. You privately slandering; you got some slick, ill things to say about your neighbor. Get away from me. Ask yourself: why do you have to privately do it?

A sensible Israelite in Christ will read that and do what? Hide himself from the evil. I don't want my name in the hat of those people that are gossipers and murmurers. I'm going to move far away from anybody that is like this. That's what you say, until it comes out that your friend's a gossiper. How do people look at you now? That's her friend. That's his boy. He must have been talking to him.

He that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight. When you don't know what you're talking about and you don't have the whole story, yet you telling it like you know what's going on, and it's not true, do you know what that's called? Oh, you thought you was exempt. It's a lie. Whether you believe it or not, it's a lie.
